description:
Insight from real usage: Claude optimizes for 'I know where to look, I'll do it quickly myself', ignoring the context window cost of sequential decisions. Need a clear rule in rules-context.md:

**Directed search** = find specific content in a known location (grep for X in file Y). Do directly.
**Exploration** = task requires synthesis (comparing patterns across files, summarizing, finding differences). Always use sub-agent.

The real trigger is not file count but task type. If the result needs synthesis - always agent, even for 2 files.

Practical heuristic: 'If directed search needs 3+ sequential tool calls OR you need to compare content from 3+ files - use explorer agent instead of sequential reads.'

Add to rules-context.md in a suitable section (near Agent Rules or as new section).
title: Add directed search vs exploration rule to workflow

description:
Brainstorm skill runs on autopilot - explorer, then 3 parallel architects (min/max/pragmatic), then review. User has no control between phases.

## Problems
1. No pause after exploration - user can't react to findings or ask questions
2. Auto-generates 3 variants (minimal/maximal/pragmatic) without asking which approaches make sense
3. Review launches automatically without user seeing architect output first
4. Violates core principle: User sees everything, decides everything

## Expected flow with checkpoints
1. Explorer researches codebase
2. **CHECKPOINT** - show findings, ask if user has questions or corrections
3. Discuss possible approaches with user via AskUserQuestion - 'I see approaches A, B, C - which to develop?'
4. **CHECKPOINT** - user picks which variants to send to architect
5. Architect develops selected variants (not hardcoded 3)
6. **CHECKPOINT** - show architect results, user picks winner
7. Final plan generation

## Key changes
- Add AskUserQuestion between every phase
- Remove hardcoded min/max/pragmatic - let exploration + user input determine variants
- User chooses how many and which variants to develop
- Each checkpoint shows what happened and asks for direction

## Acceptance criteria
- User confirms after exploration before architect phase
- User chooses which approaches to develop (not auto min/max/pragmatic)
- User sees architect output before review phase
- Every phase transition has explicit user approval
title: Add user checkpoints between brainstorm phases

description:
Two UX improvements for /lets:pr --respond mode:

**1. Multi-observation general comments**
GitHub general comments can contain multiple distinct observations (e.g. 'Phase Detection table' + 'missing /context reminder'). Currently triaged as a single item - user can only give one decision for all observations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Detect multiple observations within a single general comment (numbered lists, headers, bold markers)
- Allow per-observation triage decisions (fix/agree/disagree/skip)
- Fall back to single-item triage if structure is ambiguous

**2. Consolidated reply for general comments**
Replies to general comments (issues/{PR}/comments API) create new top-level comments - no threading. Multiple replies to the same comment create noise.

Acceptance criteria:
- Group all decisions for one general comment into a single reply
- Format: quote each observation, show decision inline
- One API call per original comment, not per observation
title: Support multi-observation comments and consolidated replies in --respond

Check what files PR workflow creates in .lets/ and evaluate each:

description:
Plan execution skill - takes brainstorm output and implements it in a clean context.

CORE PRINCIPLE: Execute runs in a SEPARATE SESSION from brainstorm. Fresh context = full capacity for code.

Flow:
1. /lets:start picks up task from beads
2. /lets:execute <task-id> loads plan from beads + .lets/plans/<task-id>.md
3. Creates feature branch (feature/<task-id>-<slug>)
4. Reviews plan critically - raise concerns BEFORE starting
5. Batch execution with checkpoints (report progress, wait for feedback)
6. Stop conditions - never force through blockers, ask for help
7. Track progress in beads comments
8. Finish with /lets:check or /lets:review -> /lets:commit -> /lets:end

Key rules:
- Never work on main/master
- Feature branch per task
- Batch execution (default 3 tasks per batch)
- Checkpoint between batches - report + wait for feedback
- Beads comments track progress (not TodoWrite)
- If context runs out mid-execution: /lets:end, new session, /lets:execute continues from beads state

Why separate from brainstorm:
- Brainstorm eats context on exploration, questions, architecture (often 50%+)
- Execute needs clean context for code - reading files, writing code, running tests
- Beads + plan file persist state across sessions
- User reviews plan between sessions (natural checkpoint)

Reference: docs/reference/superpowers-brainstorming-analysis.md
title: Create /lets:execute skill

First-time LETS plugin installation by another developer on a different machine. Goal: document every step, friction point, and issue encountered during setup. This data will be used to build an updated /lets:install skill.

## Prerequisites checklist
- [ ] bd (beads CLI) installed and working
- [ ] gh (GitHub CLI) installed and authenticated
- [ ] Claude Code installed
- [ ] Clone this repo
- [ ] Add LETS plugin to Claude Code
- [ ] Add beads plugin to Claude Code
- [ ] Add commit-commands plugin to Claude Code
- [ ] Create .lets/config.yaml manually (language, merge-branch settings)

## What to do
1. Go through the checklist above from scratch - figure out each step yourself
2. Record every step you take (commands, configs, decisions)
3. Note every friction point (unclear docs, missing steps, errors, guesswork)
4. Note what worked smoothly
5. Write down the full sequence as a step-by-step log

## Important
- /lets:install is outdated - do NOT use it
- Set up everything manually and document the process
- The whole point is to record the real experience so we can rebuild /lets:install from it

## Acceptance criteria
- Step-by-step log saved to beads comments
- Every blocker/friction point documented
- Every manual step that should be automated - flagged

description:
Utility skill (not command) that AI invokes when user wants to create a task. Handles the full flow:

**Why skill, not command:**
- Task creation happens organically ("create a task for...", "let's track this")
- AI detects intent and invokes skill automatically
- Can be called from multiple contexts: /lets:start, mid-session, /lets:brainstorm

**What the skill should do:**
1. Validate beads is available and .beads/ is reachable (handle nested repos, missing db)
2. Show available epics, suggest the right parent based on context
3. Interactive flow: title -> epic selection -> priority suggestion -> description
4. Handle edge cases: BEADS_DIR not set, nested git repos, bd errors
5. Auto-fill what it can from conversation context (e.g., priority from urgency cues)

**Error handling for nested repos:**
- If bd fails with "no beads database found", check parent directories
- Suggest setting BEADS_DIR or guide user to fix
- Don't silently fail

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Skill file in commands/ directory
- [ ] AI auto-invokes when user mentions creating a task
- [ ] Epic list shown interactively (AskUserQuestion)
- [ ] Graceful handling when beads is unavailable
- [ ] Works from /lets:start task selection step
title: Create utility skill for smart task creation

description:
Instead of hardcoded numbers (3 tasks per commit, 1 or 3 explorers), make the plugin intelligently decide quantities based on context.

## Areas to scale

### 1. Commit strategy in /lets:execute
Currently: commits every 3 tasks blindly.
Want: plan includes commit grouping strategy.
- Group related small changes into one commit
- Important/breaking changes get their own commit
- Refactoring of one module = one commit
- Plan output should include commit boundaries

### 2. Explorer count in /lets:brainstorm
Currently: fixed 1 or 3 explorers.
Want: scale based on codebase size and question complexity.
- Simple/focused question, small project: 1 explorer
- Medium scope: 2-3 explorers
- Large unknown codebase, broad question: 5-10 explorers
- Explorers are Sonnet (separate rate limit), so can scale more freely

### 3. Review agent count in /lets:review
Already somewhat dynamic. Verify and improve heuristics.

### 4. Expert count in /lets:opinion
Currently 3-5. Could scale based on decision complexity.

### 5. Batch parallelism in /lets:execute
Currently sequential. Could run independent tasks in parallel.

## Key principle
Sonnet subagents have their own rate limit - exploit this. Scale up when the task warrants it, scale down for simple things. The decision should be explicit in the plan or computed at dispatch time.

## Acceptance criteria
- /lets:brainstorm plan includes commit grouping hints
- /lets:execute respects commit grouping from plan
- Explorer count in brainstorm scales with context
- Decision logic documented in each command
title: Add intelligent scaling to plan execution and agent dispatch

description:
Rename and restructure the planning skills into a clear chain: brainstorm -> plan -> execute.

## Current state
- /lets:brainstorm = explores options, designs architecture, produces implementation plan
- /lets:execute = executes plans from brainstorm
- /lets:idea = proposed but not created

## New structure

### /lets:brainstorm (was: /lets:idea concept + current brainstorm name)
Free-form backlog population. Active brainstorming with user.
- Accept ideas in any form (text, screenshot, rant, half-thought)
- Clarify with 1-2 questions if unclear
- Recommend epic, priority, type, dependencies
- Create/update beads issues immediately
- Proactive: ask probing questions, notice connections, suggest areas user hasn't thought about
- Periodic reflection: what patterns emerged, what's missing
- Goal: FILL THE BACKLOG

### /lets:plan (was: current /lets:brainstorm logic)
Structured planning for a specific task.
- One concrete task -> codebase exploration -> architecture options -> implementation plan
- Explorer agents research codebase
- Architect develops selected approaches
- User checkpoints between phases (see 0nf.24)
- Output: detailed implementation plan saved to .lets/plans/

### /lets:execute (stays the same)
Execute plan from /lets:plan step by step.

## Migration
- Rename commands/brainstorm.md -> commands/plan.md (update content)
- Create new commands/brainstorm.md with backlog brainstorm logic
- Update all references: rules-context.md, install.md, hooks, other commands
- Update skill descriptions and skill quick reference table

## Acceptance criteria
- /lets:brainstorm = free-form backlog population
- /lets:plan = structured task planning (current brainstorm logic)
- /lets:execute = unchanged, works with /lets:plan output
- All references updated across codebase
- Chain is clear: brainstorm -> plan -> execute
title: Restructure brainstorm/plan/execute skill chain

description:
When Claude notices patterns in user's work (repeated topics, related ideas, growing areas) - it should surface this. Currently happens accidentally, should be systematic.

## Where to add

### 1. rules-context.md - universal rule
Short rule for all sessions:
- If 3+ ideas/changes touch the same area - mention the pattern
- Suggest connections between tasks
- Not pushy - one sharp observation beats five obvious ones

### 2. Specific skills (idea, brainstorm, start)
Before creating a task - check bd list for similar/related issues.
If an epic is accumulating tasks - suggest reprioritizing.
If user keeps returning to a topic - note it.

### 3. Periodic reflection pattern
In long sessions (every 5-7 interactions):
- Step back: what are we discussing most? What are we missing?
- What connections exist between topics?
- Any areas with no attention that might need it?

## Key principle
Quality over quantity. One insightful observation > five obvious comments.
Don't be annoying. Don't state the obvious. Only surface patterns that add value.

## Acceptance criteria
- Rule added to rules-context.md
- /lets:idea skill includes proactive questioning instructions
- Pattern recognition feels natural, not mechanical
title: Add proactive pattern recognition to workflow rules

description:
Improve /lets:review command with two changes based on real review experience:

1. Step 5 (agent prompts): Add instruction to all agent prompts: 'Check if the flagged pattern exists in other similar files in the project. If it is a project-wide pattern, flag it as a systemic issue rather than a bug in this PR - still report it, but clearly label it as systemic tech debt affecting multiple places, not a defect introduced by these changes.'

2. New Step 6.5 'Consistency Verification' between Filter (Step 6) and Verdict (Step 7):
- For each finding, check how it is done in other places in the project
- grep analogous files (other services, other components of same type)
- If systemic pattern - keep the finding but downgrade severity and label as 'systemic issue' with note about scope (e.g. 'found in 5 other files')
- If violation of existing pattern - raise severity (this PR deviates from established convention)

Key principle: systemic issues are still surfaced, but clearly distinguished from PR-specific bugs. The review should say 'this is a project-wide pattern worth addressing' not 'this PR has a bug'.
title: Add consistency verification and agent false positive filtering to review

description:
Add section to hooks/rules-context.md with beads usage rules learned from experience.

Key rules:
1) Epics are containers, NOT blockers - never add epic as dependency for its children
2) Only add dep when task literally cannot start without another being done
3) Use bd dep sparingly - most tasks are independent
4) Parent-child relationship uses --parent flag, NOT bd dep add
5) When creating subtasks under epic, use bd create --parent or bd update --parent
6) EVERY task MUST belong to an epic - no orphan tasks
7) If no suitable epic exists, create one first or add to closest match

Project init workflow:
- When starting a new project, AI and user should plan epic structure together
- Define 3-5 top-level epics covering main work areas
- AI should track existing epics and suggest creating a new epic when tasks don't fit existing groups
- Propose epic when 2+ orphan tasks emerge in the same area

Epic lifecycle:
- Epics are long-lived - they stay open even when all current children are done
- New tasks can always be added to existing epics
- Only close an epic when the USER explicitly says to
- Never auto-close or suggest closing epics just because children are 100% done
- AI monitors epic list and suggests new epics proactively
- Review epic structure periodically (every 5-10 sessions)
title: Add beads best practices to workflow rules

description:
Opinion analysis by 4 experts revealed pragmatist is functional but under-specified. Knows WHAT to care about but not HOW to detect it.

## Findings to address

### 1. Add model: opus to frontmatter
Pragmatist evaluates trade-offs and proportionality - needs strong reasoning model. Currently falls back to session model.

### 2. Sharpen identity - separate from architect
Current: 'pragmatic senior developer' - overlaps with architect who also has pragmatic lens.
Target: 'technical ROI analyst' - explicitly NOT a code quality reviewer. Evaluates whether effort is worth the outcome.
Add: 'You do NOT evaluate code quality, design patterns, or architecture. That is the architect's job.'

### 3. Replace anti-pattern labels with detection heuristics
Current: 'Cargo cult patterns' - sounds nice, unactionable.
Target: concrete checks the agent can actually perform:
- Count usages of new abstractions (grep). Used once = flag.
- File was split into multiple files - do new files have >1 consumer? No = unnecessary split.
- Error handling added without test exercising it + no known failure mode = speculative.

### 4. Lower confidence threshold to >= 70
The 80 threshold silences 'could be simpler' findings which is the agent's core value. Other agents (security, backend) find hard bugs at 90-100. Pragmatist's value is in the gray area (70-79).
Option: >= 70 for pragmatist only, or add [SUGGESTION] tag for 70-79 range.

### 5. Add 'When Everything Is Fine' section
LLMs force-find issues. Pragmatist must be able to say 'No overengineering detected. Solution is proportional.' A pragmatist who always finds problems is cynical, not pragmatic.

### 6. Trim expertise list from 10 to 5-6
Remove overlaps: ROI assessment ≈ overengineering detection ≈ YAGNI violations ≈ premature abstraction detection.

### 7. Add Overall Assessment to output format
Individual findings exist but no holistic verdict. Add 1-2 sentence overall assessment before findings list.

### 8. Differentiate How You Think from architect
Current questions overlap 40% with architect. Replace with pragmatist-only questions:
- What happens if we do the simplest possible thing instead?
- If we deleted this abstraction, would anyone rebuild it?
- How many people will ever touch this code?

### 9. Split anti-patterns by context
Agent is used in 5 contexts (review, plan review, opinion, brainstorm, ask). Anti-patterns should be context-aware - code review vs plan review vs decisions.

## Source
Opinion analysis from architect, qa-expert, compliance-expert, pragmatist (self-review)
title: Refactor pragmatist agent prompt for effectiveness

description:
Interactive brainstorming skill - hybrid of feature-dev structure + superpowers brainstorming clarity.

CORE PRINCIPLE: Brainstorm produces a plan and STOPS. No implementation. Clean context boundary - user starts new session for execution.

Phases (from feature-dev, adapted):
1. Discovery - clarify intent via AskUserQuestion
2. Codebase Exploration - lets:* agents (architect, pragmatist) explore context
3. Clarifying Questions - ALL questions at once via AskUserQuestion, WAIT for answers
4. Architecture Design - multiple options via lets:architect + lets:pragmatist
5. Plan Output - save to beads task + .lets/plans/<task-id>.md

Key rules:
- HARD-GATE: no code until plan approved
- Multiple approval gates (not just one)
- AskUserQuestion for structured interaction (multiple choice)
- Scale output to complexity
- Use ONLY lets:* agents
- Output is a PLAN, not code. Plan goes to beads + file.
- Ends with: suggest user to start new session and run /lets:execute

Why separate from execute:
- Brainstorm eats context on exploration, questions, architecture
- Clean context for execute = all capacity goes to code, not 'what did we decide'
- Beads + plan file bridge the gap between sessions
- User gets a checkpoint to review plan before committing to implementation

Reference: docs/reference/superpowers-brainstorming-analysis.md
